claims.text: Exceptional ethanol-oxidation performance is governed by dynamic catalyst-surface restructuring that produces local Pt-rich domains.
The Pt-rich domains remain in close electronic contact with adjacent Ru, Ni, or Co promoter atoms.
The Pt-rich/promoter configuration adjusts d-band properties to optimize adsorption of oxygenated intermediates.
The proposed surface configuration facilitates the 12-electron and 12-proton ethanol-oxidation pathway.
The proposed surface configuration mitigates catalyst poisoning and degradation.
The as-prepared Pt-based nanoscale catalyst exhibits high activity and durability for ethanol oxidation.
A mild oxidative pretreatment promotes leaching or redistribution of non-Pt promoter atoms.
The oxidative pretreatment enriches the catalyst surface in Pt.
Atomic-scale segregation dynamically forms localized Pt-rich surface domains electronically coupled to residual promoter atoms.
Oxidative pretreatment slightly depletes promoter atoms at the outermost alloy surface.
Synergistic interactions between Pt and nearby Ru, Ni, or Co atoms modulate the local d-band center.
The resulting electronic structure balances the binding strengths of ethanol and its oxidized intermediates.
Optimized adsorption enables efficient site-to-site electron transfer and complete 12-electron ethanol oxidation.
Optimized adsorption reduces the accumulation of poisoning species.
Oxidatively pretreated catalysts should have higher ethanol-oxidation current density or lower overpotential than untreated catalysts.
Oxidatively pretreated catalysts should show greater selectivity toward complete ethanol-oxidation products and produce fewer byproducts.
Oxidatively pretreated catalysts should exhibit enhanced durability during extended potential cycling.
Moderate temperature, alkaline electrolyte, and adequate reactant availability permit the proposed dynamic surface restructuring.
Extreme pH or temperature can suppress or make surface segregation detrimental.
Rapid mass-transport limitations can prevent the predicted catalytic benefits from appearing.
